title: [ ] and ( )
description:
Two more operators make a class feel built-in.

**Subscript.** Write a class `Scores` wrapping a `std::vector<int>`, with `void add(int)`, `std::size_t size() const`, and `operator[]` in **two** versions: a non-const one returning `int&` (so `scores[0] = 9;` works) and a const one returning `const int&` (so reading from a `const Scores` works).

**Function call.** Write a class `RunningTotal` whose `operator()(int amount)` adds the amount to an internal total and returns the new total. An object like this is called a *functor*: it is called like a function but remembers things between calls.
hints: Write `operator[]` twice: `int& operator[](std::size_t i)` and `const int& operator[](std::size_t i) const`. The const version is the one used on a `const Scores`.
`RunningTotal` keeps a total member; `int operator()(int amount)` adds to it and returns it.
